thread:
ash: quick follow-up from the API gateway sync — we need a concrete decision on how deadlines from clients should 'bubble' through the edge when streaming + retry/hedging are involved. cc @maria @oliver

maria: tl;dr: preserve client deadline as the canonical SLO, but gateway can apply conservative internal timeouts for hedges. need clarity on semantics for partial streams + midstream cancel.

oliver: agree on single source of truth = client deadline. where it gets fuzzy: 1) hedged requests (we spawn upstream attempts) 2) resumable streaming where we may reconnect to a different host 3) retries for idempotent vs non-idempotent ops.

kai: practical constraint: some upstreams can't honor client-level streaming cancel semantics (they just close connection or keep producing). we need a plan that avoids leaking resources or surprising the client.

ash: proposal: gateway attaches X-Client-Deadline (unix ms) header. all upstream attempts must read it. gateway enforces hard enforcement at last_message_ts (client deadline) and will terminate/return final trailer when deadline passes. before that point, gateway may spawn hedges but must ensure only the earliest successful result is forwarded.

jen: how do we handle an upstream that keeps streaming after deadline? do we force-close connection and surface grpc code 4/CANCELLED or 14/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED?

oliver: we should translate to the client's protocol: if client used streaming HTTP with chunked body, we close the stream and append a final JSON/Error chunk that indicates deadline exceeded. for gRPC we send grpc-status=4 with proper trailers. important: close path must be deterministic.

maria: about retries: if a non-terminal error occurs and client deadline still far out, gateway can retry hedges. BUT we should not restart/resume a stream from scratch unless the client asked for idempotent resume (checkpoint token). otherwise we risk duplicate side effects.

ash: agree. for resumable streaming we include an idempotency token + resume-offset in protocol. gateway will only attempt midstream reattach if token present. otherwise no automatic respawn.

kai: edge case: what if the gateway's internal retry backoff would push the next attempt beyond the client deadline? Should we short-circuit and return error immediately?

ash: yes — gateway should compute effective remaining_time = client_deadline - now. if remaining_time < min_retry_window (configurable, default 200ms) then skip retry attempt and fail fast with a transparent error indicating insufficient time for retry. This avoids wasting resources and confusing the client.

jen: metrics/observability ask: add labels for deadline-origin (client vs gateway-internal), whether a response was from hedged attempt, and whether a deadline-triggered abort happened. We need a trace/span annotation when we drop a late upstream.

maria: also surface a 'graceful buffer' config per customer: a tiny elastic window (e.g., 50ms) that lets gateway finish flushing buffered tokens on success even if the client deadline is exactly at boundary. but this buffer must not be used to start new upstream attempts.

oliver: note: that buffer can be abused; for strict SLO customers we should allow disabling it. implement as per-tenant flag.

kai: security: when passing X-Client-Deadline to private upstreams in Redwood Private, ensure it's signed or sent over mTLS only. we can't allow spoofing in multi-tenant proxies.

ash: agreed. sign the header for hosted mode using edge signing key; in private deployments, recommend mTLS + config to enable/disable header forwarding. document behavior.

maria: streaming resume protocol sketch for fidelity: client includes Idempotency: <token> and Resume-Offset: <n> as optional. gateway stores small per-session checkpoint (offset, last-ack-id). if upstream side is restarted, gateway will reattach using token and offset. We'll only attempt a reattach if current time < client_deadline. if not, return deadline error.

jen: implementation note: keep checkpoint TTL small (default 2 minutes) and limit memory per-session. fall back to error if checkpoint missing.

oliver: testing: add chaos tests where upstream ignores client cancel for a while; ensure gateway terminates and reports correct telemetry. Also tests that hedging doesn't duplicate streamed work when idempotency token is absent.

ash: follow-ups: I'll draft a short RFC with semantics, header names, config flags (min_retry_window, graceful_buffer_ms, checkpoint_ttl), and a matrix for signal translations (http->grpc->http). Anyone want to add items?

maria: add a section on billing / token accounting: if we hedge, only count tokens from the successful attempt towards customer billing where possible; if both produced tokens, prefer earliest acked window. we need rules.

kai: add a note about connection draining: when gateway drains a node, active streams within client_deadline should be remoted/handed off with resume token if available, otherwise client gets best-effort finish or cancel depending on config.

jen: +1. also include sample error payloads and best-practice guidance for SDKs (how to set client deadline and idempotency).

ash: perfect. I'll circulate RFC draft tomorrow and tag infra/console for metric names. thanks all. :thumbsup:
